name: agent-orchestration-registry
purpose: Defines the shared contract for creating many reusable agents and orchestrating them without locking the platform to one agent framework or CLI.

reader_guide.summary: Open this file before creating a new platform agent or connecting multiple agents. It explains the agent spec contract, creation blueprints, orchestration patterns, controls, lifecycle gates, and validation commands.
how_to_read: Read platform_principle to understand the design intent.
Use agent_spec_contract when adding or reviewing files under agent-platform/configs/agents/.
Pick an agent_blueprint before creating a new reusable agent.
Pick an orchestration_pattern before connecting agents or tools.
Check orchestration_controls and lifecycle_gates before implementation.
Run validation_commands after changing this registry or agent orchestration behavior.
update_triggers: A new reusable agent type is added.
Agent spec fields, metadata, or validation commands change.
A new orchestration pattern, handoff style, state model, or agent runtime is introduced.
Agent creation becomes repetitive enough to automate with a scaffold generator.
An external agent framework is adopted, upgraded, or removed.
A workflow starts coordinating several agents, CLIs, queues, workers, or merge gates.

structure_rules.rule: Keep this registry focused on platform contracts, not on a single orchestration framework implementation.
structure_rules.reason: The user wants a platform that can use many agents, tools, CLIs, and assistant runtimes without vendor lock-in.

structure_rules.rule: Every new reusable agent must select one blueprint and any multi-agent work must select one orchestration pattern before implementation.
structure_rules.reason: Agent creation should become easy and repeatable without becoming an unstructured prompt habit.

structure_rules.rule: Agent specs must include input, output, tool, policy, and validation metadata in addition to name, runtime, skills, and tools.
structure_rules.reason: Agents become hard to orchestrate when their boundaries are only described in prose.

structure_rules.rule: Any orchestration design must declare state, handoff, tool access, human checkpoint, observability, resource, and evaluation controls.
structure_rules.reason: Multi-agent systems fail through implicit state, unclear handoffs, uncontrolled tools, hidden waits, missing logs, resource leaks, and unevaluated outputs.

structure_rules.rule: Run check-agent-orchestration, list-agents, and inspect-agent after changing agent creation or orchestration contracts.
structure_rules.reason: The platform should catch missing patterns or agent spec drift deterministically.

field_guide.meaning: Plain-language operating principle for agent creation and orchestration.
Minimum fields and metadata that a reusable agent spec must expose.
Reusable creation templates for common agent categories.
Ordered steps for turning a user need into a registered, validated agent.
Framework-neutral coordination patterns for connecting agents, tools, and human checkpoints.
Cross-cutting controls that every orchestration design must address.
Stage gates that keep agent creation and orchestration auditable.
Commands that verify this registry and related agent specs.

platform_principle: The platform is not one chatbot. It is a workspace for turning repeated human work into reusable agents with explicit inputs, outputs, tools, state, handoffs, evaluation, history, and orchestration contracts.

agent_spec_contract.input_contract: Inputs must be explicit enough that another agent or UI can call the agent without reading chat history.
agent_spec_contract.output_contract: Outputs must declare expected files, structured records, summaries, decisions, evaluations, or handoff payloads.
agent_spec_contract.policy: Agent specs should describe allowed tools, source requirements, human checkpoints, resource boundaries, and close-out evaluation requirements.

agent_blueprints.purpose: Collect, rank, cross-check, and synthesize external or internal evidence before planning.
Convert evidence and user intent into plans, tasks, dependencies, gates, and validation targets.
Run scoped implementation, deterministic generation, conversion, or local tool execution from a validated plan.
Compare expected requirements, actual outputs, evidence, omissions, resources, and grounding before close-out.
Maintain durable platform rules, risk boundaries, human checkpoints, and auditable operating contracts across agents, workflows, and capability promotion.
Wrap replaceable external tools, CLIs, notification providers, or service adapters behind explicit contracts.
Create project-specific agents such as presentation, monitor, desktop, or coding project agents while keeping project artifacts inside the owning project.

creation_pipeline.description: Capture the user need, project boundary, mode, and whether a reusable agent is warranted.
creation_pipeline.required_output: request summary, ownership decision, and work mode

creation_pipeline.description: Choose the smallest matching agent blueprint and record why it fits.
Check official docs, mature frameworks, repository history, and prior agents before creating new behavior.
creation_pipeline.required_output: web search record and reusable reference notes when useful

creation_pipeline.description: Write or update requirements/spec artifacts that define the agent boundary and acceptance criteria.
creation_pipeline.required_output: spec, plan, tasks, validation, and traceability targets when governance or implementation is meaningful

creation_pipeline.description: Create or update an agent spec under configs/agents with explicit input, output, tools, policy, docs, and validation metadata.
Link reusable skills, local tools, external CLI adapters, and install requirements without hiding dependency state.
creation_pipeline.required_output: tool, skill, or adapter references plus install audit when installation occurs

creation_pipeline.description: Select a pattern and declare state, handoff, human checkpoint, observability, resource, and evaluation controls.
Run deterministic checks for the agent spec, orchestration registry, config contract, tests, and affected tools.
Keep config registries, maps, memory anchors, and project registries discoverable after changes.
creation_pipeline.required_output: updated registries or explicit not-applicable note

creation_pipeline.description: Record history, request trace, timing, omission/resource/grounding checks, and work evaluation before commit/push.

orchestration_patterns.use_when: One reusable agent can complete the task with one state boundary and no agent-to-agent handoff.
orchestration_patterns.coordination_model: Direct invocation with deterministic validation after completion.

state_contract.persistence: history or project artifact when result is durable

failure_policy.fallback: defer or ask human only for blocked decisions

orchestration_patterns.use_when: A router or supervisor must choose among specialized agents based on request type, project boundary, risk, or mode.
orchestration_patterns.coordination_model: Supervisor selects one or more agents, records routing reason, and owns final merge/evaluation.

state_contract.persistence: coordination status or plan record for meaningful work

failure_policy.fallback: record unsupported capability or create backlog

orchestration_patterns.use_when: Agent outputs must feed the next agent in a known order such as research to plan to implementation to evaluation.
orchestration_patterns.coordination_model: Ordered pipeline with explicit gate acceptance before downstream release.

failure_policy.retry: retry current stage only when inputs are valid
failure_policy.fallback: stop downstream release and record rework

orchestration_patterns.use_when: Independent agents can research, analyze, generate, or validate in parallel and a merge gate can reconcile results.
orchestration_patterns.coordination_model: Fan-out independent lanes, wait for all required lanes, then merge through synthesis and conflict resolution.

state_contract.persistence: parallel work plan and coordination status

failure_policy.retry: retry failed lane only if shared resources are not conflicted
failure_policy.fallback: merge with missing-lane caveat only when acceptance allows it

orchestration_patterns.use_when: Specialized agents may transfer control dynamically, but every transfer must preserve a bounded state contract and human-readable trace.
orchestration_patterns.coordination_model: Agents hand off through an explicit payload and policy-controlled next-agent selection.

state_contract.owner: current active agent until handoff acceptance
state_contract.persistence: coordination status or request trace for durable work

failure_policy.fallback: route to supervisor or human decision inbox

orchestration_controls.rule: State must be explicit, bounded, serializable, and tied to a source or artifact when it is used for downstream decisions.
verification: state_contract exists in the selected pattern
durable state is saved as a history, spec, config, or project artifact

orchestration_controls.rule: Agent-to-agent or stage-to-stage handoffs must include producer, consumer, reason, payload, expected output, and acceptance check.
verification: handoff_contract exists in the selected pattern
request trace or coordination status records handoff when durable

orchestration_controls.rule: Agents may only use tools, CLIs, skills, and files that are declared in the agent spec or selected workflow.
verification: agent spec tools list is updated
external CLI use references the adapter or pipeline contract

orchestration_controls.rule: Human decisions should be isolated as blocked_decision items while unblocked work continues when safe.
verification: human decision inbox is updated for pending choices
checkpoint and resume policy are recorded for interrupted work

orchestration_controls.rule: Meaningful orchestration must leave enough records to see active agents, stage timings, source provenance, outputs, and failures.
verification: coordination status or task board is updated when parallel or active work exists
work timing is recorded for meaningful work

orchestration_controls.rule: Long-running agents, subprocesses, browsers, servers, queues, caches, and streams must declare cleanup or bounded lifetime controls.
verification: resource guard is run when resource_risk_occurred=true
cleanup path and accepted risks are documented

orchestration_controls.rule: Agent outputs must be evaluated against the original request, requirements, evidence, omissions, resource risks, and grounding before close-out.
verification: work evaluator is run for meaningful work
blocking evaluator gaps are reworked before commit

required_evidence: framework or repository references when relevant
requirements or spec artifacts for meaningful changes
